fix.assertRootCause: The reduced M5/M1 CONV arm in _conv_arm (scripts/fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py, inside the mab_helper string at the patched ~L1607-1637) passed num_accepted_tokens=nacc.clamp(min=1,max=m), which drives the FLA conv-update kernel down its SPEC path. There the wrapper sets state_len = width-1+(seqlen-1) with seqlen=max_query_len=m (/tmp/vllm_live_019/vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/causal_conv1d.py:1234) and the kernel uses conv_state_token_offset = num_accepted-1 (causal_conv1d.py:859-863). The kernel's store (causal_conv1d.py:931-943, mask idx_tokens < state_len) then writes a state_len=width-1+(m-1) column span (M5 width=4 -> 7 columns) into the committed conv-state bank whose physical window is only width-1 (=3) columns -> OOB global store -> device-side assert INSIDE _causal_conv1d_update_kernel, beyond Front B host-side _guard_rows (8cdda4c4). NOTE: the FLA file the blocker named (fused_gdn_prefill_post_conv.py:215) does NOT exist in the live 0.19 tree (/tmp/vllm_live_019/...); that line is from the audit copy and is the SYMPTOM site (the next legitimate live forward's kernel faulting on the poisoned CUDA context). The arms call causal_conv1d_update (conv) + fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update (scan), not fused_post_conv_prep. The precondition violated: the SPEC-path state_len store span / conv_state_token_offset must fit the committed bank's physical width-1 column window, which the reduced m>1 / nacc>1 geometry violates.

M10 reference arm (served_geom=True) KEEPS the served spec geometry (num_accepted_tokens=nacc.clamp(min=1,max=m)) so the deep row sees the live forward's branch-co-resident sliding window (faithful, in-range by construction, untouched). Read window [0,width-1) and store span [0,width-1) are bounded by the committed bank's physical columns for ANY m / nacc / max_path_len / physical width. The deep node's true prior conv state already lives in that committed bank's width-1 window, so the reduced arm reads the correct prior context at column 0 (the receptive-field-reduced control, matching M1 = prior-window-only). This is the same pad-to-valid-shape principle the scan arm uses (torch.full valid-bank init-state, 8cdda4c4). Call sites updated: conv_m10=_conv_arm(full_rows,served_geom=True); conv_m5/conv_m1 served_geom=False (patcher ~L1811-1813).

ROOT CAUSE OF THE RECURRENCE (located, not guessed): Phase 1 forced the REDUCED M5/M1 conv arms to conv_nacc=None (non-spec, bounded) but LEFT THE M10 REFERENCE CONV ARM ON THE SPEC PATH (served_geom=True -> conv_nacc=nacc.clamp(min=1,max=m=10) at gdn_linear_attn.py:904-908/911). linear_conv_kernel_dim=4 => width=4. The spec path sets state_len = width-1+(seqlen-1) with seqlen=max_query_len=m=10 => 3+9 = 12-column store span; the kernel store mask (idx_tokens < state_len) writes 12 columns into the cloned conv_state bank whose physical window is only width-1 = 3 columns => OOB global store inside _causal_conv1d_update_kernel => async device-side assert (surfaced at the .item() sync, caught as arm-fail; symptom resurfaced at the next fused_post_conv_prep). The Phase 1 claim that M10 is 'in-range by construction because it replicates the live geometry' is FALSIFIED: the arm clones the committed width-column bank and passes qsl=[0,10] as a single 10-token request, forcing a 12-column store the live forward never does (the live scheduler bounds each request's span via query_start_loc against a state bank it sized for that). The scan M10 arm (served_geom=True, scan_nacc=nacc) is a co-suspect but the conv arms run first (1073-1075) so the conv-M10 OOB is the first/decisive trigger.
